## Problem
Once the review-kernel's downstream consumers no longer read `severity` (sibling tickets 1-5),
the review-kernel (`pass3_decide`) itself should stop STAMPING `severity` onto its own emitted
findings. `pass3_decide` has FIVE return sites that stamp `severity`
(`review_kernel/decide.py`): four via a `sev = severity_label(imp)` variable (lines 690, 706,
724, 740) and one hardcoded literal `"none"` on the no-verification/indeterminate return
(line 673, which occurs before `imp`/`sev` are ever computed).

CRITICAL MECHANISM (found by plan-review): omitting `severity` at the source is NOT enough by
itself. `code_review/shim.py::_to_common_finding` currently ALWAYS stamps a valid `severity`
via `_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY.get(raw_sev, _SEVERITY_DEFAULT)` -- for a kernel finding with
no `severity` at all, `raw_sev` is `""`, which the map doesn't recognize, so it falls back to
`_SEVERITY_DEFAULT = "medium"`. And even if `_to_common_finding` is fixed to omit the key
entirely, the finding still flows through `finalize_findings` -> `build_result` ->
`findings.py::normalize_finding`, which TODAY unconditionally re-stamps a missing `severity`
to `"info"` (`f["severity"] = sev if sev in SEVERITIES else "info"`, where an absent key
defaults to `""`, which isn't in `SEVERITIES`). So a naive "just omit it in shim.py" plan would
ship review-kernel findings that always carry `severity: "medium"` or `severity: "info"`
regardless -- silently reintroducing a meaningless label, exactly the problem this epic
retires. `normalize_finding` must be changed too: only clamp to `"info"` when a `severity` key
IS PRESENT but holds an unrecognized value; leave it ABSENT when the input genuinely has no
`severity` key. Research confirmed this is safe: no production caller or existing test relies
on `normalize_finding` backfilling `"info"` onto a finding dict that never had a `severity`
key at all (every other real producer -- `completion_reconcile.py`, `completion_child_gate.py`,
`workflow/gate_ops.py`, `spec_scan.py` -- always supplies a real severity value already).

CORRECTED SCOPE (post-decomposition research): `findings.py`'s shared `SEVERITIES` vocabulary
and the `Finding` Pydantic field are NOT removed -- they serve the completion-verification
module cluster and `spec_scan.py`, neither of which has a priority/decision alternative.
`completion_verdict.schema.json` and `review_result.schema.json` both `$ref` the SAME shared
`common.schema.json#/$defs/finding` (confirmed, byte-identical `$ref`), so relaxing that def's
`required` list technically loosens both schemas' formal requirement -- but every
completion-verification producer always populates `severity` in practice regardless of the
schema requirement, so this is a de jure relaxation only, with no de facto behavior change for
`completion_verdict`.

## Approach
1. In `review_kernel/decide.py`, remove `severity`/`sev` from ALL FIVE `pass3_decide` return
   sites: the four `sev`-fed sites (lines 690, 706, 724, 740) AND the hardcoded `"none"`
   literal on the no-verification return (line 673). Keep `severity_label()` itself as an
   internal impact-bucketing helper (still used by calibration/eval code and
   `test_divergence_grade_split.py`), just stop writing its output into the finding.
2. In `code_review/shim.py::_to_common_finding`, stop defaulting an absent/unrecognized
   `severity` to `_SEVERITY_DEFAULT = "medium"` -- when the source kernel finding has no
   `severity` key (now the normal case for review-kernel findings), omit the `severity` key
   from the output entirely. Delete `_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY` and `_SEVERITY_DEFAULT` from
   `shim.py` (their only use site).
3. In `findings.py::normalize_finding`, change the severity-clamp so it only fires when a
   `severity` key IS PRESENT on the input but holds a value outside `SEVERITIES` (still clamps
   to `"info"` in that case, unchanged); when the input has NO `severity` key at all, leave it
   absent on the output rather than backfilling `"info"`.
4. In `common.schema.json`'s `$defs/finding`, remove `severity` from the `required` list
   (leave the `severity` property and the `$defs/severity` enum definition in place).
5. Remove the vestigial `DEFAULT_BLOCKING_SEVERITIES`/`blocking_severities` field and its
   env-var registration from `review_bot/config.py` (already unused in the current
   `code_review_decision` flow per `adapter.py`'s own docstring).
6. Add ONE compatibility-note entry to `docs/release-notes.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`: `severity`
   is no longer guaranteed present on review-kernel-sourced findings within `review_result`
   (the shared schema field is now optional, not removed); every other producer (including
   `completion_verdict`'s) continues to always supply it in practice.
7. Amend `docs/adr/0108-retire-severity-label.md` with an "Amendment" section recording this
   corrected, narrower scope, including the `normalize_finding` fix.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `grep -n '"severity"' src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py` finds no finding-shape
  stamping at ANY of the five return sites (the `severity_label` function definition and any
  historical comments are acceptable).
- [ ] `findings.py::normalize_finding({"finding": "x", "dimension": "d", "detail": "y"})` (no
  `severity` key at all) returns a dict with NO `severity` key; `normalize_finding({"severity":
  "BOGUS", ...})` still returns `severity: "info"` (the existing invalid-value clamp is
  unchanged) -- both asserted by strengthened/new tests in `tests/interfaces/store/test_llm_framework.py`.
- [ ] A new or strengthened test feeds a kernel finding with NO `severity` key through the full
  production path (`shim.py::_verdict_to_review_result` -> `finalize_findings` ->
  `normalize_finding`) and asserts the FINAL `review_result` finding has no `severity` key --
  not just `_to_common_finding`'s intermediate output, so the `normalize_finding` re-stamp
  path is actually covered.
- [ ] `common.schema.json`'s `$defs/finding.required` no longer lists `severity`; the
  `severity` property and `$defs/severity` enum remain defined.
- [ ] `review_bot/config.py` has no `blocking_severities`/`DEFAULT_BLOCKING_SEVERITIES` symbol;
  `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py` and `tests/unit/test_gen_env_registry.py` are updated to
  assert the symbol's absence.
- [ ] `grep -n "_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY\|_SEVERITY_DEFAULT" src/rebar/llm/code_review/shim.py`
  returns no matches.
- [ ] `docs/release-notes.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and `docs/adr/0108-retire-severity-label.md`
  (Amendment section) each record the corrected, narrower scope.
- [ ] `make test` passes with the full suite, including
  `pytest tests/unit/test_review_kernel.py -k test_severity_label_buckets` and
  `pytest tests/unit/test_divergence_grade_split.py` (proving `severity_label()` itself is
  untouched) and the full `completion_reconcile`/`completion_child_gate`/`epic_bug_screen`
  test suites (proving the completion-verification cluster's own `severity` usage, and the
  clamp-when-invalid behavior `normalize_finding` still performs for them, is unaffected).

## Testing
Tier: in-process unit tests. Oracle (three layers, since a single-layer test previously missed
the re-stamp defect): (1) `pass3_decide`'s real output has no `severity` key at any of its
five return paths; (2) `normalize_finding` in isolation -- absent-key input stays absent,
present-invalid-value input still clamps to `"info"`; (3) the FULL production chain
(`shim.py` -> `finalize_findings` -> `normalize_finding`) fed a severity-less kernel finding
produces a `review_result` finding with no `severity` key -- proving the omission actually
survives to the schema-validated output, not just an intermediate function's return value.
Contrast/negative case: a `completion_reconcile.py`-shaped finding (always carries `severity:
"high"`) fed through the SAME `normalize_finding` continues to carry `severity` unchanged,
proving the narrower scope holds.
